targets.canonicalFact: Workspace features are verified end to end by initialising throwaway repos under a scratch KNOWL_HOME and driving the built CLI, not only by unit tests.
Knowledge-write transactions must go through the libSQL client rather than Drizzle's transaction wrapper; the Drizzle path crashed the process on bulk writes.
The write crash only reproduced above roughly a thousand writes, so small test fixtures never caught it.
The vitest suite needs its own KNOWL_HOME because suites otherwise write scratch fixtures into the developer's real home directory.
The accuracy-benchmark branch was salvaged by merge rather than dropped, on the evidence that its harness was still usable.
Export and import previously lost item lifecycle, ownership and deletions; they are preserved by a lifecycle fingerprint and tombstones.
Federated retrieval selects candidates per repo but scores every repo in one ranker, replacing the earlier per-repo fusion.
Cross-repo conflicts and duplicates are reported to the caller rather than silently merged.
A local change and a peer change occurring together were reported as one item instead of two, because the change card did not merge the two sources.
Repo discovery must skip a manifest entry whose checkout does not exist on this machine rather than returning it.
Joining a workspace had a safety gap and consumed repo names that were never used; names are now retired rather than burned.
The workspace membership test can hang past a two minute timeout, so it needs a bounded run rather than an open-ended one.
cmd.exe splits an unquoted --category list on the commas, so a multi-value CLI flag must be quoted on Windows.
promote and upgrade returned undefined for unknownIds and claimedItems instead of empty or zero, so callers could not tell refusal from success.
On Windows an absolute path passed to the Node ESM loader must be a file:// URL; a bare d:/ path fails with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME.
Search filters must be applied inside the FTS query rather than after the result cap, or eligible rows are dropped without backfill.
Retrieval reads take a store handle so they can target another repo's database without rebinding global state.
Workspace v2 blocks on a contradiction: it promises cross-owner editing while its own task refuses foreign edits, so it adds no editing capability over v1.
The lifecycle fingerprint must be derived when either side of an import lacks one, rather than compared directly.
CLI startup cost is dominated by module loading, not by work; the AI SDK imports were moved out of the main bundle to cut it.
knowl query used a different search path from the MCP query tool and was given the same engine so the two agree.
The MCP tool name arrives at the hook double-prefixed as knowl__knowl_store, so the prefix must be stripped before it matches a recorded commit range.
Repeated pending session handoff writes flood the change card, crowding out the genuine knowledge items it is meant to announce.
Workspace resolution must happen once per process rather than once per write; per-write resolution was the write-path cost.
A package that declares exports cannot have its package.json required directly; doing so fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.
A UTF-8 BOM on a hook payload makes the JSON parser reject it; the hook must tolerate a leading BOM.
Repo ownership is stamped only by the join-time backfill and never at write time, so every item written after joining has a null owner and promote refuses it as foreign.
Both bugs were found by driving the built CLI end to end, not by the unit suite.
A single foreign change is announced by both the hook channel and the MCP channel, so the same change is reported to the agent twice.
No write path sets origin_repo, so ownership is absent on everything written outside the join-time backfill.
A multi-word git commit message must be passed by file or heredoc; unquoted it is parsed as pathspecs and the commit fails.
Test suites leave scratch fixture directories behind on Windows because the database sidecar stays locked, so the run sweeps them at start and end.
